samples.identification: Burma.563-labelled DOS COM overwriting virus; SwizzleStyx display text
execution: Entry calls 0148h: AX=FA01h, DX=5945h, INT 16h requests VSAFE/VWATCH uninstall. This is not the FA00h installation query. Success is not checked.
0151h saves registers, maps ES=B800h, and repeatedly shifts text cells with REP MOVSW and 160-byte row strides. Stubbed Unicorn execution counted 2046720 writes to the video region.
0272h prints Reading system configuration, please wait. Then 0212h changes to drive root. Later 020Ah changes to \DOS.
021Ah/0246h use AH=4Eh with *.?o? and *.?x?, then AH=3Ch with DS:DX=009Eh (default DTA name), CX=0. This truncates the found file. The masks include COM/EXE but also DOC/TXT and other extensions.
MOV BH,40h / XCHG AX,BX transfers the create-returned handle to BX and sets AH=40h. DS:DX=0100h, CX=0233h writes 563 bytes of its own in-memory image to the truncated file.

The call table runs these operations multiple times in root and DOS directories. AH=4Fh calls are interspersed, but each overwrite routine starts a new find-first, so it repeatedly selects the first match instead of walking all matches. There are no checks for failed searches or already-infected files and no handle closes.
Final JMP 027Ah prints the SwizzleStyx text, falls through find-next and returns to PSP:0000h / INT 20h. No resident installation, boot-sector infection, network capability, or encryption is present.
samples.method: Complete 16-bit disassembly plus Unicorn CPU emulation. Interrupts were stubbed in Python and all memory/file effects remained simulated; successful DOS calls do not prove real deployment success. Deterministic mock searches reproduce find-first reset behavior.
samples.intent: Unprompted antivirus removal, host truncation/self replication, and screen sabotage outweigh any missing deployment context.

samples.identification: Dynamic VHD carrying a Hungarian WhatsApp JPEG/Windows-command lure and PowerShell .NET downloader
samples.container: 3 MiB logical dynamic VHD, one FAT12 filesystem. Current command member sha256 7bf749d60b27336838b44d185ebec9dc4e9dda78a17764bb4275d5403995c208. Other members are ordinary desktop.ini, WPSettings.dat, and UTF-16 IndexerVolumeGuid. MBR and volume boot code implement conventional partition/BOOTMGR reads; no virus hook was identified there.
execution: WhatsApp_kép_2026-02-23.jpeg.cmd is command text, not a JPEG. Its entry jumps through 100 assignments and shuffled GOTO labels to a line concatenating environment-variable fragments. Static control-flow reconstruction visited 307 lines and recovered the actual 6854-character PowerShell command.
The first PowerShell starts another PowerShell with WindowStyle Hidden. The inner command replaces f# with r in the assembled Base64, decodes UTF-16LE and invokes the resulting script via IEX.
Decoded code sleeps three seconds, selects TLS 1.2, creates WebClient, shuffles two download endpoints and tries each with DownloadData until one succeeds.
The response is treated as UTF-8 text. Code finds <<BASE64_START>> and <<BASE64_END>>, extracts the delimited substring, decodes Base64, and loads the resulting bytes with Reflection.Assembly.Load.

The loaded assembly is queried for myprogram.Homees, and the static runss method is invoked with six arguments including an obfuscated endpoint-like string, RegAsm, and x86. Those arguments are hints, not proof of process injection or the ultimate payload family. Process/CPU listings are interspersed as output/noise.
Payload bytes could not be retrieved. Forager attempted the Firebase object (404) and UFS fallback (403) on 2026-10-21. No final credential-theft, persistence, or injection claim is made.
samples.intent: An image-looking command lure, hidden execution, shuffled fragment reconstruction, repaired encoded script execution, and disguised remote managed payload activation establish malicious purpose despite unavailable final payload/deployment context.
samples.coverage_gap: Two distinct suspicious traits cover the original batch concealment and regex/Base64/eval co-occurrence. The substitution-wrapped encoded stage is recovered manually; the engine does not recover it as a PowerShell layer, so deeper downloader/module-loading objectives do not fire on the original container. Do not manufacture hostile counts from opaque bytes.

rule_changes.added_dos: Three hostile behaviors: self-image overwrite, antivirus-monitor removal by an overwriter, and screen rotation by an overwriter. Supporting atoms retain their own mechanics and criticality.
rule_changes.relocations: Four batch syntax population matchers moved intact to assignment/command/member source metadata. GOTO presence proves no threaded control flow; Base64-shaped constants prove no decode. Former inherited B0032/T1027 mappings were unsupported on these neutral observations.
rule_changes.severity_correction: The former ps-regex-repaired-base64 matcher also matches harmless whitespace cleanup. It is retained byte-for-byte as notable regex preprocessing in micro-behaviors/data/string/replace. The original consumer is updated without changing its boolean condition. A suspicious batch composite now requires fragment reconstruction and evaluation context in addition to the preprocessing observation.
rule_changes.severity_increase: Twenty adjacent variable expansions are a useful complete syntax observation, so the relocated atom becomes notable rather than component.
rule_changes.consumer_audit: Exact and ancestor selectors were searched in all four rule tiers. Only explicit consumers select the moved atoms. All 8 concat-file composites and all 44 batch_new composites retain equivalent conditions/scope after ID substitution. Historical migration.json is a prior accounting snapshot, not a runtime consumer.
rule_changes.external_controls: Inspected existing fixtures and searched testdata plus the named samples directory for the old regex. No independent matching positive was found beyond the same batch member already present separately at samples/7bf749d60b27. That real artifact was rescanned, and the exact matcher/boolean equivalence checks retain other consumers by construction.
rule_changes.material_detection_loss: No matchers deleted or narrowed; every original DOS observation survives. Batch syntax atoms retain detection at their corrected locations; the generic decoder/regex atom loses unsupported suspicious dropper significance. Its suspicious label disappears from the expanded batch layer alone, while the original file retains two supported suspicious objectives. The evaluated batch remains classified hostile.

verification.focused: PASS: real positive fixtures and six benign controls; matcher equivalence and all affected composite conditions checked. check.py reproduces focused scans without executing samples.
verification.classifier_gap: Atomscan 2.13.0 uses older extraction than installed Cleave 3.0.0-beta.2. Original .563 and .vhd remain type unknown with low classifier probabilities, before and after. Standalone Cleave recognizes dos_com and extracts five VHD analysis units. An exact .com copy and separately extracted .cmd are recognized and flagged by Atomscan. This is an extraction/classification gap, not grounds to weaken rules or accept the samples as benign.
